title: Every k-gonal prism is B-factorizable (Kashiwabara's Conjecture 17)
source: Kenji Kashiwabara, “Sports scheduling for not all pairs of teams”, arXiv:0809.3682 (2008); Electron. J. Combin. 16 (2009) #R55; Conjecture 17. https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.3682

significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds for every k ≥ 3: whenever a home-away pattern table for the k-gonal prism (a round-robin style schedule in which only the pairs of teams joined by a prism edge play) admits a fractional compatible schedule, it admits an integral one. The proof starts from Kashiwabara's own Corollary 9, which reduces the question to finding a compatible proper 3-edge-colouring, and then uses three prism-specific steps: the differences along the two rails alternate, the one-turn digraph of the pattern can be spliced into cycles with the right cut parity, and the exclusions on the rungs propagate around the prism to give the colouring. Kashiwabara had verified the cube (k = 4) and the pentagonal prism (k = 5) by Hilbert-basis computation. Lean states Definition 4 of the source literally (the monoid generated by compatible perfect matchings, its saturation, B-factorizability) and proves it for prism k for all k ≥ 3, together with the equivalent statement that the feasible polytope has an integral point when it is non-empty.
significance.caveat: The result is the existence of a compatible integral schedule on prisms whenever a fractional one exists, for all k ≥ 3; it does not assert that every vertex of the polytope is integral and does not touch Briskorn's conjecture for complete graphs. Kashiwabara had already verified k = 4 and k = 5. No earlier public solution was found in the sources searched; two peripheral citing papers were screened at abstract level only and one omega registry surname query was rate-limited. Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review and final check are by GPT-6.2 Sol (not routine 0.85).
